advisory.finding: Two parts of the new signal handling are never exercised. (1) Only TERM is tested, so the HUP (exit 129) and INT (exit 130) traps added in arm_lockout_notice have no coverage. (2) The `trap - ... HUP INT TERM` part of the disarm is untested: if it shrank to `trap - EXIT`, a signal between the SSM write and step 5's trap would still print the false 'interrupted' notice, and no test would fail.
scenarios: Someone changes line 108 to `trap - EXIT`. All current tests still pass, but an operator who hits Ctrl-C during the git clone right after a successful rotation sees a false lockout warning.

dropped.finding: The 'failure-after-the-ssm-write' case never checks that the script got past the SSM write. Its only anchor is `returncode == 1`, followed by absence checks on stderr. The script can also exit 1 earlier without printing the notice (missing admin key, create-account failure). In either case the test would pass without ever testing the trap removal it is named for.
scenarios: A later edit makes the script exit 1 before step 4 (e.g. a new precondition check). The test stays green, and a dropped `trap - EXIT` after the SSM write would go unnoticed.
dropped.suggested_fix: Split the mktemp case out, or add a check for it, e.g. `if steps.get("mktemp_rc"): assert (rec / "aws-stdin").read_text(encoding="utf-8") == GENERATED; assert "mktemp" in (rec / "argv").read_text(encoding="utf-8")`.
